review_notes: Read the whole file and the definitions of baseSection and IsBaseScalar (Definitions/Def_AlgebraicGeometry_DescentCharacter.lean). The `resTop` abbrev, `smul_eq` and `app_baseSection` look fine as non-simp lemmas. `app_baseSection` needs the hypothesis `hg`, and `smul_eq` is stated with `show` casts. I did not run Lean, so the claim that the two lemmas would interact smoothly under simp is untested. The finding is small and specific to this helper namespace.

findings.problem: The simp interface is placed on the intermediate definition instead of the public one. `smulLin_apply` is `@[scoped simp]`, but `smulLin` is only an internal building block of `scalarEnd`. The evaluation lemma for the exposed endomorphism, `scalarEnd_app` ((scalarEnd r P).app U s = resTop r U • s), has no simp attribute. A goal containing `(scalarEnd r P).app U s` therefore does not reduce under `simp`. It is rewritten by hand with `rw [..., scalarEnd_app, ...]` in `isBaseScalar_pullback_map`. The only simp lemma that exists, `smulLin_apply`, is scoped and never used in this file.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `scalarEnd_app` as `@[simp]`. Its RHS `resTop r U • s` is a smaller normal form, so it cannot loop. Either keep `smulLin_apply` as a plain `@[simp]` or drop the `scoped simp` attribute from it, since nothing here uses it. Keep `smul_eq` out of the simp set, because its `show` casts make it a poor simp lemma.
findings.benefit: Users of `scalarEnd` can normalise `(scalarEnd r P).app U s` to `resTop r U • s` with a plain `simp`. The `rw [..., scalarEnd_app, ...]` chain in `isBaseScalar_pullback_map` can then become a `simp` call. The simp attribute then sits on the declaration clients actually mention.
